It's a large tab, I'm afraid. I'm not going to ask you to look in a great deal of detail through this document. But on the first page of text, that's immediately after the front page, there is a list of individuals who were present at a Joint Command meeting of the Serbian forces, in this instance on the 22nd of July. And we can see there present at the meeting: Milomir Minic, president of the Assembly; Nikola Sainovic, deputy prime minister; Zoran Andjelkovic, a minister; Nebojsa Pavkovic, the corps commander; Radoljub Djordjevic, deputy MUP, Ministry of the Interior; Sreten Lukic -- and who is Sreten Lukic? Do you remember Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the name, sir, but I'm not -- I can't say under oath exactly his title, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was within the MUP, though, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I understand, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: David Gajic, assistant chief of the RDB, so presumably the line responsibility for the JSO. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Milan Djakovic, I don't know if you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djakovic, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, is this the body that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This appears to be the body for KiM, Kosovo and Metohija, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this was a coordination body coordinating the VJ and state security and MUP together, apparently?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With Sainovic, the deputy prime minister, who I think you regarded as the person being responsible for directing day-to-day operations in Kosovo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what was generally understood, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What was your reaction when you realised that the chief of the staff of the VJ was being cut out of this chain of command? What did you make of that as a Defence Attache?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I mentioned in a report that I found it extraordinary that such a powerful person who was in our -- certainly in our terminology and in Balkans' terminology, head of the armed forces, was not, in his words, within the chain of command. And it was a disturbing break with what should be normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And coming back to the answer that you gave just before the break about Colonels Zivanovic and Delic understanding the chains of command, can you help us from the description that you've given us, is there any feasible way in military terms in which the VJ's involvement in those disproportionate and destructive operations that you have described could have taken place without those two officers knowing and authorising it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why I'm delaying is just trying to think the thing through. In my military experience, the operational commander, at whatever level, has to take appropriate action if his force or his equipment is being threatened, and that is acceptable. But he is also then answerable if he has taken disproportionate action. I would have thought - and these documents are obviously new to me - that guide-lines would have been set out to ensure that disproportionate action, of whatever type, burning, looting, et cetera, were disencouraged. Let's leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I just put one rather more specific proposition to you and ask you to comment on that. I think you've said at various times that the role of the VJ in these joint operations would be to provide shelling cover; in other words, a destructive phase of bombardment before the burning started, although I think you also said that, certainly later on, there were VJ officers on the ground joining in the burning. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that appears to be correct. Through the majority of, as I understand it from what I saw in 1998, indirect fire was provided by Vojska Jugoslavije tanks and artillery to MUP operations. But sadly, in 1999 when we had moved out because of the NATO bombing, it appears that the Vojska Jugoslavije was then involved in other more direct forms of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you told us yesterday, and it may be that you corrected yourself or it was an error; and if so, then now's the time to say so. I think you told us yesterday that when you were driving through Prilep and Rznic on the way to the canal, the destructive operation that you saw taking place then was being jointly conducted on the ground with VJ and MUP forces. Does that accord with your reaction?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the -- yes, that's correct, sir. I think there were tanks there doing the destruction as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, coming back to my question, could the VJ's involvement in these types of operations have occurred without the authority of Bozidar Delic and Dragan Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You've described 52 Corps in one of your statements, you say it could bluntly be described as a village shelling force. Now, was 52 Corps located in the area of responsibility of Colonel Delic, with the 125th?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not precisely, sir. 52 Corps is the formation that was in charge of the operations within KiM, in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So have I got it the wrong way around; effectively 125th is part of 52 Corps?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does that comment that 52 Corps was effectively being used as a village shelling force a comment that would include 125th and 549th?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know the 52nd Brigade and where they were located?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of the 52nd Brigade, but forgive me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 12 years --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're asking a great deal and I don't want to -- to test your memory if you can't remember. I just want to step back for a moment from 1998 and ask you very specifically about one operation in January 1999 that you witnessed and the relevance of it will become clear, I hope, in a moment. On the 15th of January, 1999, did you witness the Serbian joint attack on Racak?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't physically witness it. I arrived in or at Racak by Stimlje after the operation had taken place. I was very familiar with the area and was appalled to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why were you appalled to see what had happened at Racak?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a very major Serbian security presence there of both artillery, I think, mortars, armoured personnel carriers, and a heavy ground presence of troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're going well past the indictment --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll explain the relevance. This operation was conducted by General Bozidar Delic, who is a witness who's coming to give evidence in this case and I want to be able to lay the foundation for cross-examination of Bozidar Delic as to his responsibility for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please activate your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry. That's a collateral attack on credit through a third witness. In my submission, the Defence have the material they need to question Mr. Delic if and when he comes and it doesn't need to be done through this witness. This witness is not going to add material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One can hardly expect General Delic to be the one to give Your Honours the proper picture of whether there were war crimes committed at Racak or not. He's--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under his responsibility, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Under his responsibility. Indeed he may have to be cautioned before he gives evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied, Mr. Re. But at the same time, Mr. Emmerson, you are invited not to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I will take it shortly. I will take it shortly. I really can take it very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to the extent needed for the purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did the operation at Racak take place under the noses of the Kosovo Verification Mission and Ambassador William Walker?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I just put it to you in a sentence. Was this an example, in your judgement, from what you saw there of a grossly disproportionate use of fire-power on an entire village in which civilians had been shot at very close range?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- the reason I'm delaying, Your Honours, is that this area is right on the edge of where there had been considerable KLA activity and MUP had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amount of force used, unfortunately, yes, I would agree, was disproportionate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would this be one of those incidents of the kind that were raised by Ambassador Walker -- I'm sorry -- by the British ambassador with General Milosevic as crimes against humanity, based on your observations?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't honestly know whether Mr. Donnelly raised this particular one. So I would suspect he did. In verification terms, it was probably the straw that broke the camel's back, bearing in mind that the Kosovo Verification Mission, which I had helped bring in in November, was an unarmed force and purely a force to monitor the situation until an event like Racak really forced a complete revision of the international community's policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just in, if you can, in one sentence, what was it about Racak that was, in your view, appalling and that caused the international community so to change their position?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the very heavy use of military force against what was a village and many people were killed. But as I caveated it before, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There was a KLA target?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- there was a KLA target within that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think you've said in other instances that the shocking thing about these operations is that you might have a small KLA operation of a few tens of men in one particular part of a village, and instead of targeting those, these operations would involve flattening the whole village. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very blunt use of maximum force, not necessarily in the right areas. But in defence of Serbian security forces one could say that they were provoked on many occasions to react, and we are in the Balkans and the person with the biggest stick, I'm afraid, beats the bushes heavier than anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I just -- is my recollection right that in a case before this Tribunal that that was never concluded by a judgement by the Chamber that days and days had been spent on evidence on what happened in Racak --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There has been evidence in relation to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want to take any further time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Because, of course, it has never resulted in any judgement on the matter. Of course, we could not just in order to anticipate on the credibility of a witness still to appear to revisit in similar detail the events and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's also my recollection that some of the evidence contradicts other evidence presented. So the Chamber would be reluctant if there is any matter which would -- would give a certain idea on the responsibilities, then we should find other ways of introducing it in these proceedings rather than to revisit Racak in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely accept Your Honour's guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want now, if I may, to turn back to your map, the map that you marked, and ask you some further questions about that. So that is behind tab 1. I've arranged for you, Colonel Crosland, and for everybody else in court to have a much clearer paper copy, and it's to your right on top of the blue file, of the map of the area as a whole that you were looking at yesterday on the screen so that you've got the two maps available to you. Now, I'm sorry, there'll be yet one further map to look at in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This exhibit that -- this map here for the record, the map that was shown yesterday on the screen without great success is P116, for the record. No. This map -- I apologise. I apologise. Colonel Crosland's map is P116. We're all, I think, familiar with the map with the rings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, can I ask you to find three hills, please. If you look towards Lake Radoniq, can you locate yourself on the map. Do you have Lake Radoniq there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Immediately to the left of Lake Radoniq is an area of elevated ground, a hill which is sometimes called Donji Bites and sometimes Radonjicka Suka and you can see it marked I think it's 571 metres above sea level. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the west or to the east?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To the west, immediately to the west of Lake Radoniq. Do you see Gramaqel?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's just to the right of Gramaqel on the map.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It might mentally or physically be helpful for you to draw a circle around this and the other two elevated positions so that we all know where we're talking about. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the map be displayed for the interpreters? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am now told it is D32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D32, it is, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have that on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You mean P --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D32, from what I understand, Defence Exhibit 32, yes. Could that be shown on the screen so that the markings can be made visible for everyone --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and that it would be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we'll need to zoom in on the lake and again and again and one more time and stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you take the pen, Colonel Crosland, and just mark -- the usher will help you with it -- in blue or in any colour -- I think blue is probably better than red so that we can see where we're talking about and draw the circle that you've drawn on the map in paper onto the screen for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just to the east of the lake can you see Suka Cermjan, which is 699 metres above sea level? It's just -- it's almost on the same latitude but just --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's it. Thank you. And then if you could please look to Gramaqel and immediately to the left of Gramaqel, can you see the words Erecka Suka, 587 metres above sea level? Now, I want to suggest to you - and if you can't remember for sure, then we can look at some of the contemporary documents to assist your memory - but I want to suggest to you that there were Serbian VJ and MUP, in other words, mixed artillery and policing positions on each of those three elevated positions.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think after the fighting I visited all three positions, yes, certainly the -- sorry, two of them. Not the one. I remember visiting Suka Cermjan as an observation post and the one just to the east of the Djakovica-Decani road. Whether I went to the other one, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it may be that you never personally went to that one, and I say that because you haven't marked that as one of the Serb positions on your map. And so it may be that the reason for that is that you personally never visited it and have forgotten about it.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I marked this map -- forgive me if the understanding is correct and we were dealing with a period in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm suggesting to you that there were operational orders of the VJ that show between the 22nd of April, 1998 and the end of September, 1998 there were VJ forces stationed on Donji Bites.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be at all surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's the high ground in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there is no way that I could have got to that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- even with copious whiskey. It was just a no-go area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I first seek clarification following. You said page 54, line 16, at least that's how it appears on the transcript. "And so it may be that you never personally visited it and have forgotten about it" which sounds --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Or have forgotten about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because Colonel Crosland was marking on the map areas where he knew there were Serb deployments --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With great respect to Your Honours and the court, I understand that we were dealing with a specific part in 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I marked what I thought were the relevant Vojska Jugoslavije and MUP security forces positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones I think we may -- I may well have forgotten about the one east of the road, okay, I accept that, but the other two, certainly I didn't see till --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- a lot later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just turn to tab 2 in the bundle for a moment, there's a large map folded over. You don't need to open that because there's an enlargement of it immediately behind the yellow card. So this is tab 2 in the green bundle. And this is a map that General Delic, as he was at that point, produced in evidence in the Milosevic trial showing deployments from the 22nd of April, 1998, onwards, through till September 1998. That was the testimony he gave about this map. And you can see that he has ringed in red Donji Bites as an area of Serb deployment?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, you personally have no recollection of that particular elevated position being used. Is that the current position, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for the reason I've already mentioned sir, is that it's a considerable distance off the road, and I would have been, A, foolish; and B, I would have been stopped by the security forces from going there for very obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just turn behind tab 3 for a second, please, which is a photograph of the canal, an aerial photograph of the canal. I'm just seeing if it in any way helps your memory. Do you see the little elevated area on the horizon to the right corner just to the left of the red letters?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now that is --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That looks like Donji Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is Donji Bites. Do you remember now whether there was Serb troops there when you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to be perfectly honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perfectly fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So one of the earlier questions you put to the witness, Mr. Emmerson, was whether the witness was aware that there were artillery positions, and then he said -- I think it was about Suka Cermjan. The answer started with "yes," but then I later understood that you went there but you saw an observation post. Is that correctly understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was an observation post when I saw it in 1999, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did -- we knew that there were heavy artillery and multi-rocket-launcher sites at the southern end of Donji -- Radonski Jezero, because they were firing over our heads into Junik, as I reported in one of my reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you did not see yourself Suka Cermjan to be a artillery post --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appeared to be an observation post, but that was not until 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Thank you very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then just -- so if I can just clarify the position, with each of those three places that you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you kindly pause between question and answer for the sake of the interpreters and the court reporter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apologies once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to draw the threads together, I'm asking only about 1998. Were you personally aware during 1998 of Serb VJ and/or MUP deployments on Suka Cermjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think we were aware of that because we could probably see them from the road. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you personally aware, yes, no, or I can't remember, I think, any one of those three, of Serb VJ or MUP deployments on Donji Bites in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we were. I think we visited that area in 1999 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and could look across and see that there had been MUP positions yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally Erecka Suka, which is sometimes called Suka Baballoq, were you personally aware of the Serb deployment of VJ or MUP forces on that elevated position during 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Could you look, please, for a moment behind tab 37. Now you, I think, have given evidence in the past about a rather incongruous tidy village along this road called Baballoq which was a purpose-built group of houses just to the east of the road. We have it on our map there, not far north of Erecka Suka. And can you confirm from that photograph that that is Baballoq?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Baballoq, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the sake of orientation, could I ask you, Witness, Colonel Crosland, and the Court to look at the face of the officer on the right back row. And then turn over the page with that officer's face in mind to see the weaponry that appears there. Can you help us, please -- first of all, what is the uniform that that group of men are wearing and the officer with the gun is wearing? Do you recognise the uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's in basic MUP uniform. As I've said on many occasions, Your Honours, that the uniform changed throughout 1999 where -- or 1998, rather, where they were specific in their details and the various more aggressive units initially were very easily identifiable by their uniforms. They then realised that people were identifying them and therefore then tried to blur the issue by using a more generalised uniform. So this is -- this appears to be a personnel from the MUP. Whether he is PJP or anyone else, I wouldn't say from this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because by later in the year, they were trying to disguise themselves as members of other units. Is that essentially the effect of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, it may be obvious to all of us, but why did you understand that they were taking efforts to disguise themselves, the members of the JSO and the PJP and the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to ask personnel concerned, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As a Defence Attache, what was your assessment at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I've just given it is that they realised that we were being able to identify units very easily with their more definitive uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to finish the second part of that, identify units as having committed crimes and they wanted to prevent you being in a position to identify them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that is what they were up to, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back to the earlier photograph of Baballoq, orientating yourself on the map, bearing in mind where Baballoq is and Erecka Suka is and with your knowledge of the area, does it appear that these officers are stationed on Erecka Suka?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the gun is that's in the photograph there, please, the heavy weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a -- it's an anti-aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's an anti-aircraft weapon. Now, let me just pick that up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could we just ask the witness -- I see on the map an elevation north of Babaloc at approximately the same distance as the elevation south of Babaloc. What makes you believe that this would be the hill you, at the request of Mr. Emmerson, circled with blue and not, for example, the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the photograph with the gang of eight or nine MUP, in the background is the main -- beyond the one, two, three -- roughly four and a half, five lines of houses, there's this very straight road between Djakovica and Decani, and therefore this would tie in with it being Erecka Suka, I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the road you see the -- well, let's say the rows of houses which are approximately white, and there's one row of houses which seems to be more reddish. Do you see that? Are you referring to the road --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road is, yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in between --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in between those two, yes. The red houses to the left-hand side of the road, and then on our side of the road, as it was, you've got the more numerous houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That should be then the road between Decani and Djakovica, I understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if I look at the map which is still taken on your screen, if I would be on the hill which is circled blue, I see the name Babaloc on the map north of that hill. If I would take a picture from that hill and have what is at least -- what at least appears as Babaloc on the map, I would be surprised to get a road of Djakovica -- Decani-Djakovica on that same photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the confusion, sir, if I remember rightly, is that Babaloc on the maps was the old village. This was a new custom-built village to house Albanians with the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This settlement was built immediately adjacent to the main Peje-Gjakove road. It's called the Baballoq settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to fully understand what is presented in this evidence, and this -- you say this is not the Babaloc which you find on the map but this is a settlement which is situated elsewhere. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Just to be clear. I don't want to give evidence myself, but I can ask Colonel Crosland to confirm it. It is related to the Baballoq that's situated on the map in the sense that it is immediately between that and the road known as the Baballoq settlement, but it is immediately adjacent to the main road, which would place this photograph as having been taken from an elevated position to its south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Crosland, do you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea when this new village was erected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, I think, Your Honour, it was erected either late in 1997 or 1998. I might be wrong there, but they erected this village, and if you look at the picture, there is a further village in the distance going towards the town of Junik, which is a similar new construction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a pretty desolate part of the world to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And, Mr. Emmerson, do we have a date --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- for this photo?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We don't, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned in passing a few moments ago, and you've mentioned in much more detail on other occasions an incident where you watched four hours of direct shelling on four places: Junik, Gllogjan, Irzniq, and Prilep. Do you remember the occasion when you watched that shelling?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it sometime during July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in one of my reports, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date, I'm afraid, escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From recollection I believe it's the 28th of July, but I'll check that when we get to the reports. Could you just describe for the Trial Chamber, please, what it was that you saw, first of all?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to recall now, Your Honours, but we had been based down in Gjakove -- or Djakovica, rather, and we drove north up past Skivjane, which I'm marking on the map, and we then turned off down either this track here or this other track here. I think it was this track here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're pointing to the north of the two horizontal blue lines that you --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- put on the map?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yeah. And we sat on this track, not hidden, plainly visible from the road, and experienced four hours of shell fire, most of it coming -- perhaps I should explain. As an infantry officer and having been under a considerable amount of shell fire myself, you can judge where the shells or where the artillery pieces are firing from. And the majority of it appeared to come from the lake area, where I've indicated, and that was going into Junik and also into Prilep and Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you recorded also Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also mentioned Gllogjan. It was -- we could see artillery hitting in the area and dust clouds coming up. Obviously, it is difficult to exactly pin-point where this fire was going to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But certainly into Junik and into Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, first of all, can you tell us what sort of weapons they were, what sort of missiles, what weight of missiles they were that were being used.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it the multi-rocket-launcher is 122-millimetre which produces a large shell, and there was also indirect fire coming from other positions, both artillery and mortar positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the heaviest of those weapons, what -- just give us a sense of what kind of damage one shell would cause, what area of damage it would cause.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the -- if they were using 155-millimetre guns, they would create a crater the size of the area in front of us; if it was slightly smaller, the crater would be smaller. But they would do very considerable damage into civilian -- primarily civilian areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Emmerson, I think the witness --"the area in front of us," --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we agree on a diameter of approximately 5 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that's one shell?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long did the shelling go on that you watched that day?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think if I recall correctly from my reports for four hours, because it was transmitted both direct to my ambassador in Belgrade and back to the -- to the Ministry of Defence in London over secure telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because I think you had a satellite phone with you and regarded the situation as one of such urgency that we -- did you not speak directly to the Foreign Secretary Robin Cook?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was relayed directly to him. I didn't have the honour of speaking to him himself no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And why was you that you regarded that particular incident as requiring ministerial attention?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, sir, because at that time -- this was in July, I think, as you said, our parliament and our masters that be are tending to go on holiday, which is quite rightly their prerogative. What I was trying to impress on people was that the situation in Kosovo was becoming extremely critical and that people might take it into their minds that when the international community was on holiday they would commit further crimes. So that is really why I placed more emphasis on it than the normal amount of chaos that was going on down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, this is obviously a very inexact topic that I'm about to ask you about because you can't possibly know the exact number, but can you give us a sense of the frequency during those four hours, the number of shells you would expect in the broadest possible terms to have landed, for example, on Rznic and Gllogjan area or the Junik area.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really answer that question, sir, but all I can say is that Rznic and Prilep, certainly Prilep off the road, was about 18 inches high. Now, this is not the first time that Prilep had been hit. As I've said before to the Court, destruction had been carried out in a major way to many of the villages throughout the province of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you yourself saw Prilep subsequently, did you, and it was flattened to the level of about 18 inches high?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I think somewhere there are photographs. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, just from a military point of view, what is the -- I mean, are we looking at more than one of these heavy weapons firing simultaneously, or are we looking at one firing and then being reloaded and then firing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would suspect they're usually deployed in a battery of either six or maybe a half battery of three, usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was this firing continuous for four hours or were there --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- long breaks?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- if I recall right, sir, there was about four hours firing of all the natures of ammunition, both tank, artillery, rocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think the rockets towards Junik passed directly over your head. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's more or less correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we can see where you were, they were coming certainly from the east of the road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were coming from the area where I drew on the map, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you just point me to that again.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in -- it was in roughly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- area here, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make pauses between question and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can we note that this now --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- is a double ellipsoid marking south of the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, the marking at the bottom tip of the lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I also ask you to direct the witness to -- we get now a lot of blue circles on the map and at a certain moment it will be quite a job to find out which is which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So put some letters on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you put a letter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps first do the -- first series is the identification of the three positions, that is Suka Cermjan and the other two hills. If we make that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour think that the locations themselves would need an initial? Because it would be reasonably easy to see what those circles are indicating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- I leave it in your hands. But if --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, the critical numbers are number 1, please, to show where the fire was coming from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and number 2 to show your own position.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the artillery and rocket fire appeared to be coming from this area here. There was other tank fire also going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 1 is not that clear. The 1 is the very small vertical line just north of Zdrelo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if you could put a 2 in the position where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned to the Court, it's one of these -- these two lanes. I think it was this top one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I cut you off just a moment ago. You said there was also tank fire and other fire. Where was that coming from?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to be coming from this area down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a 3, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. And that was directed in which direction?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was going towards Junik primarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So the range of these weapons is sufficient, is it, to reach the distance from Lake Radoniq all the way over to Junik, these heavy weapons that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Will we save this?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Later on we'll deal with all the other exhibits in the binder, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but for the time being, the marked map, that's map D32, but now marked by the witness. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D36, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I add one question. What's the maximum range of the weaponry you noticed that was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, tank fire can go to about -- between 3 and 5 kilometres, usually in the area of about 3 kilometres. Artillery fire can go probably 10 to 15 kilometres, and multi-rocket-launcher has got probably a maximum range of about 22 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you look behind tab 25 in this bundle, please, the one right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That for the record is 65 ter number 858, because as I say, we'll collect all the exhibits in the bundle with proper numbers in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it refers to the document urgent to the command of 52 Battalion, police -- military police battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we -- before we continue, Mr. Emmerson, you earlier started asking our attention for the person on the photograph with the nine people before the new --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Baballoq settlement. You then said look at 37a. You have given that up. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, no. The point about the photograph is so that you could see that the second photograph is taken from the same position as the first photograph, because it's the same man --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you are giving evidence. I don't know for the same position yes or no. But you started asking our attention for it, and we didn't hear any further from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, the witness has given evidence about the uniforms that were being worn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And about the weaponry and about the location in the second photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll check that. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Can I be clear, do you have tab 25? This is a heavily redacted document.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Brit Mil Rep.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's the one. If we could just look at the summary. It's dated the 28th/29th of July. Tour taken by UCK north of Orahovac to Malisevo --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you go on, these are under seal. Are these being publicly displayed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday we didn't do them in e-court. We did them by handing around the court. This may well be being displayed publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have no need for it to be displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will instruct AV not to show any of these documents. That means that we can use them on the screen. A video redaction will be made, Mr. Emmerson. The document will not be further shown on the screen, and AV is instructed to proceed in this way. Would you please keep in mind that whenever you're using any of these documents in e-court that everyone is alerted that it should not appear for the outside world. I take it you understood that, even if it's shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I didn't ask for it to be shown. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's why we've got them all in paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Emmerson, the interpreters have not been provided with a copy of it. So if we don't use the screen, then they are not able to read it. Let's proceed. I think matters are clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'll read the passage into the record, but we'll arrange for the interpreters to have a copy immediately after the next break. It should have been done now. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The way we are proceeding now also works, but it just should be clear that what is on our screen will not be broadcasted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, probably while that's been going on you've had a chance to cast an eye over this document, have you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do see there first of all in the summary a few lines down: "Junik under artillery, tank and mortar fire from 1300 onwards. Unanswered questions ... where is the civpop from Orahovac." And then at the bottom of that paragraph: "How do Serb authorities explain wanton damage to towns and villages." If we turn over the page, if you look just below halfway under "comment," there is a reference to Lapusnik junction. That's just roughly halfway between the punch-holes. At Lapusnik junction one strike force of approximately 150 mixed SAJ, PJP and VJ and APCS" -- that's armoured personnel carriers, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- "gathered to launch an assault on Malisevo. "Commander of the force somewhat surprised to see tour arriving." Now, that's Legija, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's as I understand it, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's that incident. And then you carried on from there, it seems, at 3: "Turned west on main road in direction of Peje." And a little further down under "Comment: Every village from Lapusnik westward has suffered deliberate damage by cannon and HMG fire." Is that heavy mortar guns or --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heavy machine-gun fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Machine-gun fire. "Many houses burning. Garages and businesses trashed." And then just at the bottom of that page, 5: "Junik area. Tour heard and observed fall of shot into Junik throughout the PM," the afternoon, "of the 28th of July from line of sight approximately 4 kilometres' distance, also heard MBT" --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main battle tank, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- "and APC," armoured personnel carrier, "HMG/cannon fire together with MORs" -- mortars, presumably?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- "tour denied access to the area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that assist you with the date on which this heavy fire that you've described took place?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we can take it that the heavy fire that you saw on Irzniq, on Prilep, and on Junik on the same day was an incident that took place on the either the 28th or the 29th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of July. Thank you very much. What I'd like to do now is just to take you with, I hope, reasonable speed through some of the other DipTels and documents in this bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honours just give me one moment to organise myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, you used the expression "direct" and "indirect fire." Could you just explain very briefly what the distinction between direct and indirect fire is.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Direct fire, sir, is that that comes directly from the weapons system concerned, whether it's a main battle tank, heavy machine-gun, anti-aircraft fire directly on to the target itself; and therefore, it presupposes that the person firing the weapon can actually see the area they are engaging. Indirect fire is used for artillery or mortar fire that's usually firing from a greater range, not necessarily, but it may be that the target itself is difficult to pin-point and therefore they use artillery and mortar fire. So that is what we call in the military indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And will be directed on to the target by people possibly closer or who can see the fall of shot or the fall of strike of the rounds or the bombs bursting on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as a layperson, one would imagine that indirect fire is less accurate than direct fire. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not necessarily, sir. If it's controlled properly, then it is as -- it is as good as the person who's controlling it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could -- and you saw, I think, both forms of fire on the day we've just been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes, we heard them, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you please turn now behind tab 4 -- and as I say, what I want to do now really is to move through these documents but dealing only with certain passages. Now, tab 4 is a sitrep that you -- I'm sorry, that was filed on the 8th of March dealing with the incidents at Donji Prekaz that you gave evidence about yesterday, and I'm not going to ask you to repeat any of the evidence that you gave yesterday about that. But can I just seek clarification on one matter --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't seem to have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 5.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, tab 4, I apologise, tab 4. Does your -- I think that may be it. Is that a sitrep for the 8th of March?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1630 on the 8th, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can I just ask for this clarification. You mentioned Likosane and Prekaz. Can I jog your memory in this way. The incident at Likosane took place on the 28th of February and the incident at Prekaz about a week later on the 5th of March. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you attended both of them, is that right, in the immediately aftermath?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the immediate aftermath, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us yesterday about the bodies that you had witnessed at Prekaz. Can I ask you, please, to tell us a little bit about the bodies, if any, that you either witnessed or learned about at Likoshan. First of all, Likoshan was the site of the Ahmeti family compound. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it right -- and I'm going from one of your own statements so -- if that assists your recollection. Is it right that you learned that 16 people had been killed, that ten people had been seen leaving the village alive, but that those ten people were then subsequently found dead?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written in my statement. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see any of the bodies at Likoshan, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I think if I recall right, we drove to the village of Likosane and we saw the graveyard where the bodies had been placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Just to be clear, what is the significance of the ten people having left the place alive and then having been found dead, as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The indication is that they were murdered by someone after they left their village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that at Prekaze you had seen a lot of very, very close head wounds that suggested that people might effectively have been put to death. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- yes. It is unusual to see so many powder burns on people's heads and faces, indicating that there may well have been foul play.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If we can just turn over to the top of the second page of this sitrep, you've observed there in the second line: "Worryingly, there are few reports of wounded, which would be expected, given the intensity of some parts of the conflict." Can you explain the significance of that remark.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think based on my own combat experience, you have an engagement between adversaries, one side wins, there are several fatalities, and there are usually a fair amount of wounded people as well. It just seemed odd to me that there were no wounded perceived at this particular spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do I understand from that that you inferred that there was at least a significant risk that the wounded had been put to death?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be alluded to, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this I think, as far as you were aware at least, this was not an operation that the VJ were involved with. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, sir, I don't think they were, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the JSO, Frenki Simatovic's organisation, they were involved. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir, because I wasn't there. I can't say that under oath. That's -- unless I made a statement to that fact, you are asking me to recall -- I think my first statement was in 1999. So if I've made a statement to that effect, then I would stand by that but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, to be fair, what your statement on this says in relation to Prekaze is: "I photographed the bodies. I believe it was the MUP and the PJP who carried out the operation, and I suspect the JSO, RDB secret service armed forces and SAJ anti-terrorist forces were involved too. They were the only units trained to carry out such a house-type assault."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I mean, that is referring to Prekaz.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did ask about Likosane, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's entirely my fault. May I clarify the question then in two stages. First of all, in relation to Prekaze was it your understanding that the SAJ and the JSO had conducted the close-quarters operation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect that that is what has happened, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is there any comment that you can make about that one way or the other from a military perspective about Likosane?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I can't, sir, not under oath, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for clarifying that. I think, though, you did see, didn't you, caterpillar marks on the ground within metres of the Jashari family house in Donji Prekaz and within metres of the Ahmeti house in Likoshan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would indicate the use of armoured personnel carriers, probably being used in a direct assault mode --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which provides protection, sorry, for the troops about to assault the house which -- if in their opinion - and I can't -- I can't give that opinion - they needed protection, then it is a sensible use. Why run across the open ground and get shot when you can arrive there in an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How close were the vehicles to the house?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Houses --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in the two incidents.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. At the Prekaz area, I believe they were literally within metres, 4 or 5 metres, if not closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we infer from that that the troops must have gone into the property, as opposed to having a fire-fight from a distance?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in general terms, sir, they would have put down what we call covering fire from a distance to allow the assaulting troops to get close, and then on a coordinated basis the covering fire would have switched to other targets, possibly people running away or whatever, and then the assault would go in conducted by the assault troops closest to the objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you mentioned yesterday that there were bodies of the elderly and children amongst the victims at the Jashari incident. Can you tell us whether the pattern that you observed of powder burns indicating close fire were evident on the bodies of the elderly and the children.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am trying to recall from a long time ago now, sir. I think it was a general remark across the majority of the bodies that I saw, but I am -- as you know, I'm not a pathologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, they were -- there was a baby killed in that incident, wasn't there, a child under 3?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of an anti-terrorist operation, would it be classic tactics to move in in order to decapitate an organisation by taking out people who were thought to be its leaders?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, yes, sir, but there are different ways of doing operations. I mean, this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously, it wouldn't be a legitimate operation to kill children at close range; I'm not suggesting that. But I'm trying to analyse what took place. From the point of view of the SAJ and JSO anti-terrorist operations, strategically would it make sense to take out the families of the Jasharis and the Ahmetis if you thought that they were potential leaders of a movement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were fortunate enough to get a group of them in a isolate -- relatively isolated house, as this was, then it would be a very lucky and unusual circumstance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it's a circumstance that was characteristic of the Albanian resistance movement, isn't it? There were families, like the Haradinajs, like the Ahmetis, like the Jasharis, who were together in one place at one time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's indicative of the way of living of the Kosovo Albanians, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the 28th of March they moved in to the Jasharis -- 28th of February, I'm sorry. On the 5th of March, they moved in to the Jasharis in Prekaze.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on the 24th of March, there was an incident in Gllogjan where an attack took place on the Haradinaj family compound. I think you said yesterday that at the time you were not aware that the Haradinaj family compound had been attacked. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what I said, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But could we just look behind tab 8, please. This is your DipTel for that day, and it's another one that you asked to be passed immediately to the political director --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: We're not sure if we have the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have -- behind tab 8 I find --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did I say 8? I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a daily report of the 27th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Completely my fault. It should be behind tab 5. That was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This document also should not be shown to the outside world. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'll read it slowly for interpretation. "Summary: Several serious incidents today, including fatalities, at least one operation appears to be continuing. Special police units much in evidence, but still no signs of active VJ involvement." Pausing there. When you use an expression like "special police units," what does it encompass of the groups that we've been describing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the elements of the PJP and the JSO, SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So despite the fact the JSO are not technically police --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- but security service, but that generic expression covers all of them. "Decani," paragraph 2, "my DA has confirmed local media reports of exchange of fire in several villages between Decani and Djakovica. According to radio Pristina," there's then an explanation from the Belgrade media about the incident having begun with an opening of fire on a police patrol. And then just picking it up at the bottom. "My DA has reported that at approximately 11.30 shots were heard in Rznic from a police helicopter. There were two explosions followed by an exchange of fire lasting 20 minutes." Of course, Rznic is closer to the main road than Gllogjan, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considerably, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The incident that is being described there by reference to the Belgrade media certainly appears, on its face, to be a reference to the attack on the Haradinaj family compound. And I'm just wondering whether that prompts your memory in any way?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem as the -- I mean, this telegram is actually written by my ambassador and therefore is covering nearly the entire province of Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I think, if I might say so just to inform the Court, there were incidents going on throughout Kosovo which we were involved in. So most days were extremely long.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 3: "Kosovo information centre close to Rugova's LDK have condemned the police action, alleging that some villages were surrounded and houses set on fire. The independent Albanian media is reporting that three houses were destroyed. There are also Albanian claims that villagers have fled the area. It appears that the operation is still taking place and that the area has now been sealed off." Again, can you remember being denied access to that area or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, sir, it -- this telegram is covering a good --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- deal of Kosovo. Where exactly we were at what specific point, apart from the timings, as they are put here which are correct, I mean midafternoon we were between Pristina and Pec at Kijevo --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where there were problems. So it gives an indication of just how disparate the incidents were around the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock and at same time I would like to have a clarification. You said, and the witness confirmed that, that Rznic was closer to the main road than Gllogjan. Was your question about as the crow flies or -- because then I have difficulties, at least if you are referring to the main road between Decani and Djakovica, it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it wasn't a question asked as the crow flies. Let me -- may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you mean that the -- of course I can see on the map that if you go from Gllogjan to the main road, whether you take Dubrava or Rznic, that it will all be a longer distance than if you go from Rznic directly through Prilep to the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's what you meant and if that's what the witness had in mind when he answered your questions, then there's no further --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask Your Honours just to turn to the witness's own marked map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because I think it's probably the clearest way of looking at it behind tab 1. And as soon as I've dealt with these questions, perhaps we could take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, you've got your own marked map there, I hope. That's Colonel Delic's map, I think. Yours should be behind tab 1, unless it's moved. Did you take it out of the bundle when you were looking at it earlier on? If it's not there, take mine, that's unmarked other than your markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just gives witness this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can just find Irzniq and Prilep, you've drawn blue circles around Irzniq and Prilep; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To indicate on this map that they were not within the area of influence because they were disputed territories. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prilep certainly was a disputed area and was levelled, as we've agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rznic was, I would say, on the edge of -- of the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the edge of the area.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And therefore ebbing and flowing in the way you've described?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And coming from the main road, would you go through Irzniq to get to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The point I would make to the Court is that one didn't know whether mines had been put in the countryside around the area and therefore you kept to the roads that the locals used for obvious reasons, that they would be safer than going cross-country to these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we can see Gllogjan there. Did you know incidently when you went to the canal that that canal flows right through Rznic and within a hundred metres of the police station there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you proceed, I earlier said that I would verify the facts on the line of my question that you didn't give a follow-up to 37 and 37a. I checked that. What we have now is a photograph of seven people of unknown date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have another photograph where at least at first impression it looks at as if the man behind the gun is the one who appears on the upper row to the right-hand side in the other.
