It seems -- I mean, I can imagine that it makes sense to produce this evidence if there's evidence that - we spent a lot of time on Babaloc - that the gunman is at that same hill, but I think that's not part of the evidence led until now. If it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I meant when I said there was no follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there's also --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- no evidence yet on whether the one picture is -- even if we don't know when it was taken, whether at least it dates of approximately the same time as the other one, even if it's unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. There are unanswered questions about those photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I accept that. Your Honour, in the photograph showing the gun, Your Honours will be able to see the mountain range --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in the background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The higher mountains, yes, yes. I've noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For those familiar with the region, its location is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- not a mystery, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But not being a mystery is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, and I said that there will inevitably remain unanswered questions about those photographs. What we -- and if I could just return to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll keep matters short.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seemed that when I put the question to you that you seemed not to fully understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where my problems were. It seems now that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you would understand where the problems are.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. There is material in this bundle which will answer questions of locations of Serb troops but if I can back to Your Honour's point from this -- from when we first sat, I think it's most unlikely that I will complete -- be in a position to complete my cross-examination this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- made that observation at the very beginning and that has not changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, just before we leave this document, the sitrep from the 24th of March, when you gave evidence in the Limaj case -- and for those following the transcript, it's Limaj 1870, line 23 to 1871, line 12, you commented about this sitrep and about the incident in Irzniq where there's a reference to a police helicopter and so forth and you said that you had personally seen houses in Irzniq on fire on that occasion, on the 24th of March. Can you now remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I mentioned it in a report dated that particular time, sir, then that will be factually correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That isn't in fact in your report. It was in the testimony that you gave in the Limaj trial, that you had a recollection of seeing houses on fire in Irzniq on the 24th of March. I just wonder whether you can help us with that now. It may well be that details can't all be recalled.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be perfectly honest, sir, without referring to my tour schedule, I suspect that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say under oath that it is definitely correct, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And just one question before we move to the next document. From a military point of view if you were to establish an artillery position on an elevated location, first of all presumably the purpose for doing that is because you've got the best possible view of the area you wish to dominate.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from a military point of view it would make logical sense, would it not, for the VJ/MUP joint forces to locate on the three hills I drew to your attention if they wished to dominate the area which they regarded as a KLA stronghold in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could -- they could dominate the area by having the ability to see during the day. It doesn't necessarily mean to say they could see during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Did they have night vision equipment or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I'm aware, in great quantities, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But nonetheless, if one was planning the positions from which to locate troops, one would seek out the high ground, wouldn't one?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's dependent on where -- whether your enemy has got the ability to fire back on to your positions, which are obviously a lot more obvious --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on those that are hidden on what we would refer to as a reverse slope so that you've got some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But in this instance, as you've already told us, one of the peculiarities of this asymmetrical conflict is that the KLA had no ability to fire back and in this area were located in flat lands?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's more or less correct. They didn't have it at this particular time in March, no. They later acquired rocket-propelled grenades which could have inflicted some damage, yes, later on in the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I -- could you just tell us -- because you referred us to Limaj's testimony 1870, line 23 to 1871, line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said, you put it to the witness: "And you said that you had personally seen houses in Rznic on fire on that occasion on the 24th of March."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we would find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If I misquoted the witness, then I'll correct myself but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the witness said from what I see is that he's -- the question then was: "At this time did you -- the report refers to Rugova complaining about houses being set on fire. Do you recall seeing that at all in any of these villages at this time?" And the witness said: "Yes, this was to be a sad reflection of the whole conflict" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- "throughout 1998" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "And I think later on I mention that something like over 200 to 400 villages were purposely and wantonly destroyed by the Serbian security forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's the following question and answer. "And on this particular occasion you saw these houses on fire, you saw these houses being fired? "A. Yes, we did, sir." And that's referring to the 24th of March DipTel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'd like to have that verified because on this specific occasion after you have talked about 200 and 400 villages, it's far away from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- date --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- 1870, line 5 "on the 24th of March do you remember this particular incident? "A. Yes, very well."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's more than one page before that where a lot of other water has gone over under the bridge. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Since Your Honour has raised the point, 1871, line 1, just 10 lines on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the question is -- the answer is "Rznic is to the east of the major town of Decani" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: --"there are still very small hamlets. At this time did you," and so on. In other words, it's -- the line of questioning seems to me to be perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the answer goes to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- other--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it reflects what happened on 200 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or 400 villages so there -- I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then back to the specific of the particular occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could verify once. Mr. Crosland, where you just said that you -- testified that you personally in Rznic houses on fire on the 24th of March, I checked your testimony and one could say that that's what your testimony is, but at the same time there are a lot of other villages mentioned as well. Could you tell us whether you remember 24th of March, Rznic, house on fire -- houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you put the -- your finger on it. If I've written it in a statement, then I presume it is true, but I've given so many statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's oral testimony in January 2005.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that is what I said, sir, under oath, then I would presume it to be true, but I would need to check my tour schedule. As I've tried to indicate to the Court, we were travelling throughout Kosovo all this time, going from one disaster area to another. So I may have made a mistake, I may not have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that you made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I understand, sir. But there were -- at times it seemed that Kosovo itself was alight --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just go back to the line of questioning I was pursuing with you about high ground and low ground. You told us earlier in your testimony that because the KLA were located in difficult areas for an insurgency to operate, namely flat lands, they would be relatively easily overrun. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general military terms, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on how your tactics are developed and that is where there are a lot of unknown factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Faced with an insurgency and a concentration around the headquarters in Gllogjan with the ability, in effect, to move around the countryside, from a military strategic point of view, would it make sense to locate your artillery on the high ground in that context?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, sir, if you were happy or content that they were not in threat of attack, then the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And certainly from the period from April through to September in western Kosovo, that would be the position, would it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: These particular artillery positions that you've mentioned, and there was a further one that I referred to in Decani which also had on the high ground by the hotel a battery of six light artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I ask you about that. There was a high ground position near Decani monastery. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- the monastery's on the right-hand side of the track leading down to it. You go further along the track and you then turn up the hill past what was a hotel, which became a special forces base. And then you went -- we drove into the artillery position which overlooked Decani and other areas of western Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that again would have been a strategy of locating their artillery positions on high ground?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Generally speaking, was that their strategy, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to be, because obviously their thinking out of the problem was that they could not be attacked on these positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can we be a little more specific by explaining what is "their positions."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm referring to the Serb forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And they -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and I think the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And what forces and -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question again just to make it absolutely clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, can you confirm that it was, generally speaking, the policy of the VJ forces in collaboration with the MUP forces to locate their artillery positions on high ground in western Kosovo during 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is more or less correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned a hotel near Decani monastery, and that was used as a barracks for the JSO to operate out of, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the personnel that I saw on the -- I think on the one occasion I got in there, because they certainly weren't letting me in again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a very sensitive target area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. So you only got into the area around the monastery, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We went down to the monastery. I can't remember whether we went to visit one of the brothers there, which we had done in other areas. We then decided to turn up towards the hotel. There was a barrier across the hotel entrance, if I remember correctly, and we then went up to the other barrier, which was manned by a VJ soldier and we spoke to him and drove in, and to our surprise, we found ourselves in a full-blown artillery position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I was going to ask you. Were the JSO then protecting VJ artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's correct at all, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So could you explain --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VJ -- the battery position of the six guns was guarded by Vojska Jugoslavije.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So could you just explain what you meant in terms of the proximity conjunction between the JSO that you saw and the VJ artillery position.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the JSO had chosen the hotel for obvious reasons, because there was better accommodation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they let the Vojska Jugoslavije man their artillery positions, which obviously needed to be in open ground in order to place the six guns of the battery concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and they were further forward on the hill, whereas the hotel, to my recollection, is actually slightly on the sort of back-side of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And why did it come as a surprise to you? What was it about the situation that was surprising?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was surprised that we got in so easily to a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the JSO were surprised that our vehicle had turned up there anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember now roughly when in 1998 that was?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in one of my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Can I be clear. Do I assume from your answer that you didn't know in advance that there was either a JSO contingent there or indeed a VJ artillery position there from the intelligence that you had?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think if I recall from memory, we hadn't got that intelligence then, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does in a tend to suggest that it was earlier in the year?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was earlier in the year, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just clarify one other question about artillery positions with you. Generally speaking, let's assume, for example, there is an artillery position on Suka Radonjic that we've looked at. Generally speaking, in a position like that, presumably some form of ground defence needs to be established to prevent an insurgent force from surprising the artillery position over land by making their way up and launching an attack on it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly within the British army we employ that type of tactic, yes. The artillery have a job to do and they're usually guarded by numerous soldiers who are there for that particular job.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is there a concept of having some sort of cordon sanitare around an elevated artillery position so that you can be sure --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the principle in the British army. If I recall rightly, I don't think that was -- I don't think that was very visible. I mean, they had -- in this particular position at Decani there were shell scrapes, you know, shallow trenches around the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- those could have been for the artillery personnel themselves to live in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Generally, let's assume for a moment that there was an artillery position in Suka Radonjic, the hill that we see in the photograph of the canal. Generally speaking, would you expect the Serb forces to maintain some level of control on the land around that to ensure that they couldn't be attacked?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that would involve presumably sending ground troops on to the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think one of the big mysteries of the war in the Balkans is that the tactics employed by, shall we say European armies, is not necessarily being employed by Balkan armies. And one of the peculiarities was that on very few occasions did either side, whether it was in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, or in Kosovo, did either side really close and engage in what one would call hand-to-hand fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And therefore a lot of the principles of protection around defensive positions were not alluded to. So there might have been people around this position, there may not have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we just have a look behind tab 7 just as an example of the sort of thing that we're talking about for a moment. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before we do that. I'm trying to understand your last answer, Mr. Crosland. You said: "And therefore, a lot of the principles of protection around defensive positions were not alluded to." Now, earlier the questioning was quite clearly about this Radonjicka Suka. Did you intend to say by this answer that you would consider such a position as a defensive position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was both a defensive position and an observation position, Your Honour, because of the height that it was involved and the area it was looking over towards, in particular towards Junik. As I said, the -- some of the procedures that were carried out by the Vojska Jugoslavije were perhaps not as thorough as are normally carried out by more conventional armies, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that I introduced that element of uncertainty, because I was using Radonjic Suka as a hypothetical example; of course, this witness's evidence is that he can't remember whether there was or wasn't an artillery battery on Radonjicka Suka on the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, of course, quite a lot of questions are put to this witness which I would say are not exclusively questions on facts but include --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- some expertise as well. I have asked myself several times whether as a matter of fact we are listening -- of course we are listening to a witness of facts but also to a witness who gives a lot of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So to that extent, it's to some extent also expert testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not complaining at all. I wanted to make sure -- and if I might just engage to this extent in a dialogue with the Court. I wanted to make sure that there was no misunderstanding about Colonel Crosland's evidence about defensive positions, because I don't think there was a suggestion of defensive as opposed to offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's answered my question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 7 -- so I was asking you about the risk of attacks on Serb artillery positions. Now, you've told us that there was a powerful Serb artillery position in the south end of Lake Radoniq, powerful enough to reach Junik, because you saw it yourself. If we just look at this sitrep very briefly, I think it was mentioned yesterday in passing. This is the 28th of April sitrep behind tab 7 in the green bundle, for the record. In paragraph 2, four lines up from the bottom: "A four-hour fire-fight near Lake Radonjic between Decani and Gjakove on Saturday evening apparently left no casualties." Did you do any follow-up in relation to that at all, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this telegram is signed by my ambassador.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And therefore may well have been culled from all sorts of sources, like Beta, LDK, et cetera, media, that was now starting to come into the operational area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So not necessarily, if I can put it this way, a Colonel Crosland observation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not unless I was there at the time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it does appear, though, that there was some sort of an engagement between the KLA and the Serb forces at that artillery position that you describe as having been the source of the attack on Junik, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might well have been. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to look behind tab 8 for a moment. This is an ECMM report from the day before. So it's an ECMM report behind tab 8 dated the 27th of April. If I can just pick it up at 3, first of all, paragraph 3 under "security." "There has been a significant increase in VJ and police presence" --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. Before you go on, this one is displayed. Is that being publicly displayed? It's a Rule 70 ECMM document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that all documents are not publicly displayed, Madam Registrar. Is that correct. It's confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, "There has been a significant increase in VJ and police presence in Djakovica itself with one instance of masked possibly special police identified patrolling by vehicle in addition to other armed patrols and spot police check-points."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Did you see masked police officers, police officers wearing masks at all while you were on your tour of duty?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And dropping down a little bit, if I may, to 4(B): "Of particular concern to local members of the LDK is the presence of Serb artillery units in the area of Lake Radonjic north of Djakovica, which is a firing point from which most villages in the area of Decani can be found." A little bit further down at (C): "Evidence of Albanian families fleeing from the Decani and border region to Djakovica was given to the team with lists of approximately 4.000 Albanians now in the city." And then if I could just ask you to turn over to paragraph 6 -- sorry, I apologise, paragraph 9. "An armed Albanian group fired at VJ soldiers located close to Lake Radonjic near Djakovica on April the 25th. The attack started about 9.00 and lasted more than four hours. The VJ returned fire but there were no casualties. The VJ assumed that the target of the attack was the pumping station by the dam." And just finally on this, if I can. I'm not going to ask you a specific question on this document, but I wanted you to look at another one first. And behind tab 9 is the VJ report on this very incident that you've referred to in your sitrep --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, sorry to interrupt you. May I just ask, as to the document we have just seen, the witness to explain us how we can -- if he has seen this document before. Please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't recall this document because it's an ECM document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have seen it. I'm sorry. You know, I've seen an awful lot of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And may I ask you: How do you know it's an ECMM document? Because it's from MT Belgrade. What does this abbreviation say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a very good point --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think something's been chopped off here that makes it an ECMM document, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do you know what "MT" would mean? This is monitoring team or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may well be monitoring team, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It may.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is one of a number of ECMM reports served by the Prosecution on the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Right. Yes, we can -- we will be able to identify that. I just wanted to make my life easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And similarly behind tab 9 is one of a number of Pristina Corps command orders and reports served by the Prosecution on the Defence, and bearing in mind that it is a draft translation only that's been served so far. Behind tab 9, Colonel Crosland, is referring to the same incident, apparently, on the 26th of April, a report as a -- listed as a very urgent report to the command of the 3rd Army and the PRK from Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Djordjevic. First of all, do you know what PRK stands for there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume it means Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And so that would be a report back from the field, presumably, to the Pristina Corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And we can see there: "Between 9.30 and 10.30 at night on the 25th of April in the redeployment area of the 52nd BVP, Military Police Batallion, defending Lake Radonjic, a terrorist infantry attack was launched from the direction of Zdrelo village. The attack was repelled, after which the terrorists ceased firing." Now, a couple of questions, if I may, first of all. The 57th Military Police Battalion, was that an artillery unit, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The 52nd is a military police which had been used for protection, I presume, of the very large multi-rocket-launcher and artillery position that was in -- as I indicated on the map, that was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So would they then be the sort of ground protection groups that I was asking you about earlier on?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be for a target as valuable as a multi-rocket-launcher and artillery position. They could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And so just to return to the questions I was asking you earlier on, would you expect those people to be deployed on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson. The point I'm making is that in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make pauses between question and answer for the interpreters and the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. In the best world, yes, you would like to have protection wherever you went. Sometimes there are not the troops available; but on a target of this nature, I'm not surprised that the police battalion was there to provide protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Zdrelo I think we can see on our map with the red circles on it is just to the south of Lake Radoniq. So can you see that? It should be circled in fact.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's south of the -- south of the lake -- the dam itself, and presumably defending entry to that area there is a tarred road, if I remember rightly, up there Janos, which leads to the lake in -- roughly in which area we were stopped when we attempted to go up there, and we were not able to go up the unmarked road from Bec [Realtime transcript read in error "Pec"] to Zdrelo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then was stopped by who?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: By military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be clear, Serbian military personnel?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the face of those reports, it would appear to have been an attack launched from the south towards that position?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a -- a position that can inflict severe damage, and therefore a high-priority target.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, presumably you would regard it as an entirely legitimate military objective, to take out a weapon that was used to raze villages like Junik in the way that you've described?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I say, it's a high-priority target, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we turn back to tab 7 for a moment and to the tab that's numbered 7a within it, because this is another DipTel that was sent on the same day as that one but dealing with different subjects. And if we could just very briefly look at paragraph 3, which I think we might have touched upon at some point yesterday. "Beta," B-e-t-a, "a local independent news agency is reporting that eight Albanians were killed in police activity against the village of Gllogjan near Decani, widely believed to be a KLA headquarters." And I think you said yesterday that Beta was a reliable source. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perceived to be a reliable source, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to relate this, if I may, back to the evidence you've given about that map that you drew a red line on and the way in which it's been used by the Prosecution to suggest an area of exclusive control. Because this would seem to suggest, wouldn't it, that you were reporting a police attack in which eight people were killed in Gllogjan itself on the 28th of April?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, with respect, sir, what one -- I feel you're aiming at is that the place was a no-go area. Now, I didn't indicate -- if I indicated that, then I apologise. But the reason I said that the KLA were in this area -- I did actually say that they did not own it, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what I'm trying to say is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, please don't think I'm criticising you, Colonel Crosland. I'm not criticising you at all.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that the situation was extremely fluid through the whole area and incidents happened, several in a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Just so there's no misunderstanding, in the course of the questions that I'm going to be asking you about this, I'm going to be taking you to a series of incidents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you are speaking at a speed -- speaking at a speed --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That can't be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you now and then look just straight ahead and you see the transcriber sitting there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I clarify something so that you understand the drift of the questions I'm asking you. I'm not suggesting for a moment that you have ever said anything inconsistent about this, but your map has been represented by the Prosecution as a central part of its case theory that the KLA was in exclusive control, on the basis of which the Prosecution seeks to suggest that bodies found in the canal within that area must be KLA victims even if their identities were unknown. And since you've already told us that that was not what you said or meant to say about the map, what I'm seeking to do with you - and I'm going to, I'm afraid, have to do it through a number of documents over the entire indictment period - is to draw to your attention a series of incidents and clashes within that area which demonstrate that, quite contrary to the theory that the Prosecution has imposed upon your map, that there were Serb forces operating within that boundary. So it's not a criticism of you, but it is a question of clarification for the Trial Chamber of the reality on the ground as per your own reports of instances that were taking place there. So no criticism expressed or implied at all so far as you are concerned, if that's the way in which you had understood my question. So just to revert in relation to that paragraph, paragraph 3, that is you reporting police military action in the village of Gllogjan itself which resulted in fatalities, as reported by a reliable source, as far as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This telegram is signed by Ambassador Donnelly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's his assessment through Beta and he says: "I will be visiting that area today." So it's not -- it does not come from myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From yourself at all.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it was -- I think your evidence yesterday that Beta was a source regarded by the embassies --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I mean, Beta and other -- Koha Ditore and other places -- other papers were used as a source of eliciting information from the Kosovo Liberation Army and their supporters, which obviously was not given that easily at times.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I turn now to tab 12, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can we before we leave that document --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- ask the witness if you have remember to have produced some follow-up report yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: As it was said: "My DA will be visiting the area today."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, paragraph 4 talks about a Japanese diplomat who was fired at at Lausa, which is in the Drenica; and if I recall rightly, I think I was actually asked to go down there to speak to the people concerned and see whether we could make certain this lady was okay. So -- again, another very busy day. So I'm not certain whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- it will be within my reports or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we turn then to tab 12. And I want to just ask you about this document for a moment. Now, it relates to the situation in Ponosevac at which you -- we looked at very briefly yesterday, and if you'll recall, the screen wasn't clear enough for us to mark the position at Ponosevac reliably. If you'd like to look at the big map with the red circles on it just to orientate yourself again. Did you have an area that you referred to in your reports as the Ponosevac-Junik triangle?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that an axis that really ran from Gjakove, north towards Ponosevac, and then up to Junik, and then back on to the main road. Is that the triangle?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. It takes the road that comes south and then west through Korenica, on up to Ponosevac, Molic, to Junik, and then back to the main road between Decani and Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I then look, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, yesterday 's transcript that I only read. You say from Gjakove north to Ponosevac --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Does Your Honour see the road, it runs north in a westerly direction -- in fact, perhaps it's west and north or north-west. It's a yellow road marked on the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I considered that to be more west than north, but okay that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And -- yes. Sorry. Well, perhaps I should simply put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The three points of the triangle are: Junik, Ponosevac, and Gjakove --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that correct, Colonel Crosland?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is describing the situation on the ground on the 11th and 12th of May. "Situation in Ponosevac area very tense. Area in Ponosevac-Djakovica-Pec-Decani patrolled by elements of JSO and PJP in a very heavy-handed way. Villagers have fled north to Junik. Main road Pristina-Peje still closed." I'm not asking you about that but about Ponosevac. And then in the "Details" section. "Ponosevac: Road south to Ponosevac carpeted in empty cases, including 40-millimetre grenades. Villages south of Ponosevac deserted. Livestock slaughtered in fields. Houses sprayed with gun-fire. Ponosevac empty except for JSO/PJP, who are carrying out patrols from Decani using APCs including TABC-79 and IPR, similar to M-60. Most villagers now concentrated in Junik, about 3.000 with enough food and water but no telephone." And then "Comment: This JSO-PJP operation is perhaps to freeze this known transit route and cut off supplies to UCK in Jablanica." And then just over the page, if I could, paragraph 7, "Assessment: Situation could rapidly spin out of control post-ongoing talks if Serbian security forces feel that they are losing control. Heavy-handed terror action in Ponosevac area indicates that the tactical thought process has not changed." Now, a number of questions about that, if I may. First of all, when you say -- or when the report says that the road is carpeted in empty cases, including 40-millimetre grenades, do you remember this tour?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, very precisely. We left Djakovica on the western road going towards Korenica, which was Vojska Jugoslavije position from time to time, and from there on in, as I indicated in the -- my report, the road was literally covered in empty cases. And around the corner came these armoured personnel carriers firing their machine-guns, to which we waved to them to desist. The reason I mentioned these armoured personnel carriers is these were the ones that were taken from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I was going to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's why they were of interest -- particular interest as to where they had got to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: These armoured personnel carriers, if you can help me with this, are the ones you could recognise that the Dutch UNPROFOR had stolen from them in Srebrenica in 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what we confirmed later on in the -- when we got back to Belgrade, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dutch UNPROFOR had stolen them?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, had had them stolen from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, had stolen from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In Srebrenica in 1995 - obviously we're all generally aware of what took place there - but as part of that sequence of events, a group of armoured personnel carriers were stolen by the Yugoslav forces from the Dutch military. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was part of an operation, was it, in which the Yugoslav forces pretended to be UNPROFOR forces in order to facilitate a massacre?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was part of the [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so they took the Dutch vehicles away with them.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And those very vehicles you end up seeing in the hands of the JSO and the PJP in Ponosevac area in May 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you report that back - presumably you did - to the VJ or any --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did report it to the VJ and I sent it in a -- well, this report here, although signed by the ambassador, was sent because I was still down in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, again I said to you much earlier on that, quite apart from the assessments that you'd made at the time that the paramilitaries who'd been involved in the slaughter in Bosnia had re-appeared in Kosovo, there were indications along the way in your sitreps. I mean, did you regard this as an indication that there was a line of continuity between those involved in Srebrenica and those involved in policing western Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, with respect, sir, that would be a very -- I couldn't say on oath that that is -- I mean, I take -- I follow your questioning. But for me to state that the same people had been involved in Srebrenica is not -- I cannot do that under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But somehow those vehicles had ended up in the hands of the JSO?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's why it was of interest, because the Dutch warrant officer, I think, was with me on that particular tour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was Frenki Simatovic, the person who was the head of the JSO in western Kosovo, was he involved in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at Srebrenica, sir, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 40-millimetre grenades, again just to be clear, what fires a 40-millimetre grenade?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can have a grenade launcher which discharges grenades, I suppose, roughly the size of my clenched fist which are, again, destructive weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I understand this. You said that there was a burst of fire when you turned around the corner. Was that directed at yourselves or was it part of an ongoing operation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't particularly know. We just made it very clear who we were and we'd rather they didn't fire at us, to be quite honest, in an unarmoured vehicle or in any vehicle for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, there were no civilians there at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no civilians there, sir, no. The amount of destruction in this particular area was absurd. I don't believe there were any livestock left, as I think I've indicated in my report. Most of the houses had been badly, badly damaged, both by -- I suspect by both tank fire, by the size of some of the holes, and normal anti-aircraft fire and heavy machine-guns carried by these armoured personnel carriers. So it was an open display of terror, is the word I would use, to frighten off any remaining civilian population, if they were still there, out of this area. I mean, this area is close to the Albanian border, and therefore understandably of significance to the Serbian security forces from a point of view of security, but there are ways of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was this, in your assessment, an example of the Serb forces creating what you've described as a free-fire zone?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is more or less correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you just explain to the Judges what it was you were referring to in previous testimony when you said that on occasions the Serb forces would create free-fire zones?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these areas, anything that was standing, any crops that were on stalks of hay or any buildings, any businesses and normal houses would be fired at and left in a very damaged way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, is it in part to drive out a civilian population so that they can operate freely militarily without shooting people in the cross-fire. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose, in defence of the Serbian forces, they were attempting to clear the way between the normal villagers, the Kosovo Albanians or Albanians, and those who were interested in Kosovo Liberation Army activities. It's a very heavy-handed way of doing things, and obviously in the long run does not generally bring you into good repute with the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this, when you say it indicates this -- sorry, in the "Assessment" at the end you say: "This heavy-handed terror action in Ponosevac area indicates that the tactical thought process has not changed," what did you mean? Has not changed from what?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, sir, the -- one of the ongoing practices of the war in the Balkans has been the exchange of fire into civilian areas at range rather than the willingness to confront opposing armed forces, whether military or paramilitary or terrorists, whatever you want to call them, in a -- what one might call a more soldierly-like way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can we look behind tab 14 now, please. This is a VJ order. I just want to deal with this briefly with you, if I can, please. If we look at page 6, it's signed by Colonel Dragan Zivanovic. It's a 125th Motorised Brigade command order, and it orders certain deployments. And if I could just ask you, please, to note the date, the 16th of May. So this is just a, I think, five -- four or five days after the observation that you'd recorded in Ponosevac. I'm going to put it to you shortly and then take you to the passages. This is essentially a VJ operation moving south from the Decani area; in other words, coming in the opposite direction. And I just wanted to ask you just to confirm that for us, please. If you look an page 2 -- I'm sorry, I do apologise. I've given you the wrong -- I think I may have given you the wrong reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you refer to page 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes -- no, I'm sorry. May I stay with this document; it's not the document I've just summarized. I do apologise for that. It's a different document but no less relevant. It is an order from Colonel Dragan Zivanovic. It is dated the 16th of May and it is a 125th Motorised Brigade command document and it's behind tab 14 of the green bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at page 2, this is one of those documents that relates to the deployment of VJ forces in the area around the lake. "BG2," that's Combat Group 2, "is to be ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along the following axes: The barracks-Smonica village-Ponosevac village-Gornja Morina village" -- those are all areas towards the border, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then this: "The barracks-Erecka Suka." Do you see that reference?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "And the barracks at Radonjicka Lake." Do you see it on the following line?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does that appear to be an indication that the 125th had barracks at Erecka Suka as well as at Radonjicka Lake?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes. But it does actually say "redeployment," so where they were redeploying from is not clear -- certainly not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But certainly on the face of this by the 16th of May that is the position?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's as stated in this order, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then it says: "Task in cooperation with neighbouring forces of the Republic of Serbia MUP, break-up Siptar sabotage and terrorist groups and secure supply routes for VJ units." Was this, the 11th -- the 16th of May, was this at a time when the VJ was still denying to you that they were doing joint operations with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, sir, there was not a recognition of it until Colonel-General Ojdanic gave the briefing to the Belgrade attache corps in late August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the face of it -- you say there wasn't a recognition of it. You were raising it, though, from time to time, weren't you, and being told that there was no such collaboration?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was quite -- yeah, it was clear to me that there was collaboration, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it was being denied is the point I'm making?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this appears to be an order by Dragan Zivanovic specifically authorising his troops to conduct a joint operation with MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- as stated here that's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Next: "BG3 is to be at the ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along the following axes: Pec-Decani-Rastavica-Junik-Ponosevac." So that would be areas to the west of the main road, radiating out from Decani all the way down through Junik to Ponosevac; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- appears to be correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then also from Pec to Zahac, Klina, Iglarevo, and a third front from Pec to Rausic, Barane, and Celopek; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is stated here, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to confirm, and again please do not assume any kind of criticism of you because there is none, but can I ask you to confirm that Barane and Celopek are within the area you've marked in your red marking on the map?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me, I need to find where these particular places are.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Just give me a moment. Well, Barane is -- if you look at the road -- you know where Ljumbarda is?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not a term I'm familiar with --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, if we can -- let me not take time on this at the moment because we are -- it's towards the end of the afternoon. We can all check the map later on and confirm that that's the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Emmerson, I'd like to better understand. I see a native-English-speaking counsel examining a native-speaking witness. BG2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I read that: "... is to be at ready in the current the redeployment sector for operations along the following axes." Please correct me when I'm wrong. I understood an axis to be a line --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- around which something happens. Now, "axis" is used here in the plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the barracks, Smonica village, Ponosevac village, Gornja Morina village. So the barracks is one point and then three other points creates, perhaps, a line. And then a new -- what seems to me to be a new axis. The barracks, Erecka Suka because then it's a - how do you say? - a semicolon, and then again barracks through the village and then the barracks Radonjic lake. Now, please correct me when my understanding of your native -- of your language is wrong, but it appears to me that axis are described -- several axes, among them the axis: Barracks-Radonjic Lake, which of course is different from any suggestion that there would be barracks at Radonjic Lake but that there is a line to be drawn between the barracks --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do not know what barracks and Radonjic Lake, just as there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- supposed to be a line drawn between barracks, I don't know which one, and Erecka Suka. Correct me when I'm wrong, but you agreed so quickly on -- that this language suggests -- and of course I haven't seen the original, it's just the English translation, that this suggests that there is barracks at Radonjic Lake or Erecka Suka, which I have difficulties in following. But I immediately admit, it's not my native language so I could be totally misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand exactly the point Your Honour makes. I don't think it's a linguistic issue, if I may say so, it's a question of interpreting what the text means in -- you know, without any linguistic subtleties. The position is we know that there was a Serbian fixed deployment at the lake because the witness saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, but the Chamber doesn't know that. So if you are interpreting these matters without further explanation on the basis --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of existing knowledge, that doesn't assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No -- well except that in understanding what the punctuation is intended to convey, the witness's own knowledge - and indeed Colonel Delic's map which shows deployments both at Erecka Suka and the south of the lake, is an indication as to how one would interpret the punctuation. I mean, I'm not -- it's not a linguistic indication, but if we know there is a barracks or a deployment at Radoniq Lake and we've seen a map from Colonel Delic saying there's also one at Erecka Suka, then it may well be that the punctuation is indicating that there will be deployments into those areas and that's it's dealing with Erecka Suka -- an axis between Erecka Suka and Radoniq Lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all fine. I can read a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I can see what's on the map. Here I've got language in front of me. So if this adds anything, then it's not by imposing what's on the map in this text -- although you could combine them and say that is how it's understood, but at this moment it's just language for me. I'm looking at the clock --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's almost 7.00. There's one issue ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we also could ask the witness. You have followed the brief discussion I had with Mr. Emmerson, where I wondered whether the text really tells us what you seem to agree upon rather quickly. Having heard this discussion, could you tell us, Mr. Crosland, whether it's on the basis of your knowledge that you interpreted the text in this way or whether you could assist me in -- as a native English speaker, in better understanding this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think what Mr. Emmerson is trying to portray, if I may, is that the operation order that this document currently refers to is what the brigade commander, or 125th commander, was either tasked or wished his troops to carry out. And therefore, these objectives on the various axes, as you rightly acknowledged, are areas of operation into which this particular formation was going to be tasked to go. Now, if I may, I don't know whether I recall there being -- the last axis I've now found and become more familiar with the map. I recall an excursion from Pec southwards into this area. Now, whether they got as far as the objectives that are outlined in this document, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not that much interested in what happened, but rather on what the document tells us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think, with respect, sir, it is that -- what Mr. Emmerson is saying is that these are the objectives and this is what was potentially achieved. Now, it may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But still then the question is: What the text tells us about what the objectives are --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we -- yes, if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Simply this, Your Honour. That this -- General Delic is the 549th. His map shows that his troops are based at Erecka Suka. This is the 125th, which is further north, and what this telling you is that the 125th is going to be deployed from its barracks to Erecka Suka --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, that's your interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and from its barracks to Lake Radoniq. So you've already got the 549th at Lake Radoniq because that's the map that Colonel Delic has marked as being there from the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And here they are being joined by forces that are intended to pursue an axis from their barracks down to those fixed positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, I'll re-read the transcript precisely over the weekend and see whether it needs any further clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, we have not finished your cross-examination, unless -- the Defence has not - and we have three Defence teams - have not finished your cross-examination. We are informed that you're not available Monday next week --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but that there's a fair chance that you would be available in two weeks from now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's -- Your Honour, that is correct. I'm not available for two weeks, and I then need to look at my commitments there on in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Crosland - I'm looking at the parties - but most logical seems that we would then continue cross-examination at a moment that Mr. Crosland is available again. At the same time, Mr. Crosland, at this moment you've started your testimony; That means that, and that's also my instruction, not to speak with anyone about the testimony already given or still to the given. That means for further communication, you should speak with the Victims and Witnesses Section, who will be -- who will liaise between the Tribunal and yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the Victims and Witnesses Section has your data so that they can reach you if need be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is -- then I suggest that you inform the Victims and Witnesses Section about your commitments after two weeks and that the Victims and Witnesses Section informs the Chamber about availability, and that we'll then see when we would like to see you back. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's perfectly understood, sir. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Emmerson is on his feet, Mr. Harvey is on his feet, Mr. Guy-Smith not yet but just one word is good enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd simply like to say obviously we are all extremely grateful for the witness's cooperation, and may I make a plea to all concerned for the witness's testimony to be resumed at whatever is the earliest possible resumption date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one very small transcript correction but it could cause confusion at a later stage. I just draw people' attention to it so that it can be checked, as the witness is here and it's going to be some time before he's back. On page 104 at line 10, the witness referred -- said: "We were not able to go up the unmarked road from" -- and the transcript reads "Pec," P-e-c, "to Zdrelo," where it's clear from looking at the map that he meant Bec, B-e-c. Just that minor correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if I could thank you, and we expect you back soon. There is one procedural issue I would like to raise for one second. It will not take us more than one minute, but you are excused. Madam Usher will escort you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one issue which seems to be resolved, that is, whether or not the 92 ter statement, that's the -- the 92 ter statement of the 19th of April, whether that would be tendered, yes or no. Just for transparency reasons and to have everything on the record, I see in the transcript of yesterday that, although these words are attributed to Mr. Emmerson, it is clear that Mr. Re is speaking. It says: "I received an e-mail from Mr. Zahar saying you had ruled against me, and I wasn't -- I hadn't tendered it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That does not reflect what the e-mail says, Mr. Re, because the e-mail says: "The Judges have asked me to inform you that the Prosecution should proceed with Crosland's examination-in-chief as if the motion for admission of the 92 ter statement has been denied." We then invited the Defence, to the extent possible, to immediately give any reasons for objections. We were informed that there were objections. We also understood that the Defence received this e-mail too late still to respond. But then later in the e-mail it says: "The Prosecution is invited to make such adjustments in order to see whether finally the 92 ter statement may be allowed into evidence at a later stage." So if it's on the record that we had ruled against you, the Chamber found itself in a rather awkward situation where we were provided with a 92 ter statement at a very, very late stage and where we could not ignore the possibility that there would be an objection, but we did not know exactly what these objections were. So we had to give guidance to the parties as to how to proceed, and that's not exactly as you presented it on the record. Yes, Mr. Emmerson, I'm not seeking to start any debate on the matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, neither am I. But I think it's incumbent on me to record, though, that in light of that position I raised it yesterday afternoon so that I would know before starting cross-examination what the case was that I had to meet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the position now is that the application is withdrawn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, it's withdrawn --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and it's finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But just the withdrawal, it looks as if it is because the Chamber had already decided that it would not accept it, and that is on the basis of this e-mail not what happened. But it's withdrawn so there's no need to further revisit the matter. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not litigating it. I just, obviously, misinterpreted what the -- what the e-mail said. And my interpretation was that when I said we are going to proceed on the basis that it was denied, that at that point there was nothing I could do, other than to proceed on the basis that it was denied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, some suggestion was made there on the basis of perhaps hearing from the Defence what the reasons for their objections were, and that while leading the evidence that you might overcome some of these objections, for example, by giving a further factual basis for certain portions of the 92 ter statement. Let's not further litigate the matter, but the Chamber is -- would like to have this clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course, but I just want to add that we did inform the Trial Chamber that everyone -- I can't remember the exact time but last week, that we were intending to produce the Thursday before the following paragraphs in 92 ter form; and to those we added I think about four paragraphs from the one we received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- clearance from the British government on Tuesday. So we gave advance notice of our intention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, when --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and rang you on the morning. I rang you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you except the -- and then you expect the Chamber to do all the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that everyone did act in the best interest of this trial.
